title: The Margin Kept Back on Open and Assessed Equipment Rental and Demo Agreements
content:
Kit that is not yet back at a counter, and kit a technician has already faulted, both leave the collective exposed beyond what the agreement shows it owes today, and the amount kept back from the security hold is taken at a multiple of what is left.

## The rule

Where the rental account carries an assessment against an item on the agreement, and the agreement stands with the kit handed in, the amount kept back is the assessed retention multiple of what is then left. The assessed retention multiple is 125 per cent.

Where the agreement does not yet stand with the kit handed in, the amount kept back is the open retention multiple of it. The open retention multiple is 150 per cent.

In any other case nothing under this heading changes the multiple.

## The two conditions in combination

| The agreement stands with the kit handed in | An assessment stands on the rental account against an item on it | Multiple applied to what is left |
| --- | --- | --- |
| yes | yes | 125 per cent |
| yes | no | nothing under this heading |
| no | yes | 150 per cent |
| no | no | 150 per cent |

The open row does not ask about assessments at all: an agreement that does not yet stand with the kit handed in is taken at 150 per cent whether or not anything has been found against it.

## Worked figures on a hypothetical agreement

Take an Equipment Rental and Demo agreement where 180.00 USD is left when this heading is reached.

- The agreement stands with the kit handed in and an assessment stands against an item on it: the amount kept back is 125 per cent of 180.00 USD, which is 225.00 USD.
- The agreement does not yet stand with the kit handed in: the amount kept back is 150 per cent of 180.00 USD, which is 270.00 USD.
- The agreement stands with the kit handed in and no assessment stands against it: nothing under this heading changes the multiple.

## Point of judgement

**Which standing is looked for.** What is looked for is the agreement standing with the kit handed in. An agreement standing overdue, cancelled or uncollected does not stand with the kit handed in.
